div.data-meta-description: Learn about the Critical Humanities Commons Hub and Lounge, view the spaces, and find information about booking an event.

div.p: Reserve the Commons Hub, Lounge, or both for your event.

Located on the third floor of the Clearihue Building in room C305, the Commons evokes the spirit of its original architectural design as the heart of the Faculty of Humanities. The space is freely available for Humanities Faculty and Students for booking events, in consultation with the Commons Director.
The space is divided into two sections:

A multimodal space accommodating up to 50 people, equipped with accessible meeting technology, including ceiling-mounted microphones, an 180-degree camera, and whiteboard screen. The Critical Encounter speaker series will be hosted here, along with other Commons programming. Seating can be reconfigured to match event needs as required.

div.p: A welcoming collective area designed for informal social gatherings, open dialogue, and interdisciplinary exchange. The Lounge is a flexible, inclusive space where faculty, students, and visitors can meet casually, host drop-in conversations, or engage in spontaneous collaborations for teaching, research, creative, or community.

div.p: The Critical Humanities Commons is committed to making our space as welcoming and accessible as possible. All hosted events are hybrid for increased inclusion, with opportunities for audience participation. Auto-captioning is provided for virtual audiences and displayed clearly in the physical space. For Lansdowne lectures, we strive to provide ASL interpretation.

The Commons is on the third floor of the Clearihue Building in the C wing. There is an elevator located just outside the Commons’ main entrance, on the left; across from the entrance is administrative assistant Sarah Lawrence’s office. Washrooms are down the hall, to the left of the elevator. An accessible and all-gender washroom is available on the first floor of the Clearihue Building; a full list of all-gender washrooms with menstrual products is available on the campus website.

We welcome participants to share any access needs or requests in advance by emailing Sarah. At the start of an event, we will additionally review our accessibility provisions and respond flexibly to access needs as they arise.
We recognize that accessibility is an ongoing practice and are committed to creating a more inclusive space for everyone.
